clue.text: A Tory held in affection in the recess

indicators.note: the Tory's letter is held within the word for affection, cutting it open after its first letter

parts.note: affection means love
C is short for Conservative, the party of the Tories

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician being fondly regarded during the parliamentary recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recess' tempts as the parliamentary holiday, but here it is a nook in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a nook set back into a wall, a synonym for a recess.

clue.text: Problem causing endless trouble for Costa Rica

indicators.note: trouble means to stir up, so these letters are stirred into a new order
endless means the last letter of Rica is cut off

explanation.surface: Something causing unending difficulty for Costa Rica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts RICA to RIC; 'trouble' rearranges COSTARIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a word puzzle, and a puzzle is a problem to solve.

clue.text: Prudence is an amusing person

explanation.surface: A woman named Prudence is a funny character.
explanation.definitionFit: Caution is carefulness, and a caution is also an old informal word for a comical person.

clue.text: In other words, cited evil wrongly

indicators.note: wrongly means incorrectly arranged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone misquotes a passage about evil.
explanation.definitionFit: Videlicet, abbreviated viz, is Latin for namely, used to introduce a restatement.

clue.text: He breaks the code of a Guard

parts.note: taken as written
a fender is a guard, as round a fireplace or on a car

explanation.surface: A security guard is accused of breaking the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who breaks the law or a code of conduct is an offender, a lawbreaker.

clue.text: European aviator whose landfall in Norway was noted

definitions.text: whose landfall in Norway was noted

explanation.surface: A pilot from Holland whose landing in Norway was set to music.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner's opera of this title opens with the ghost ship landing on the Norwegian coast; 'noted' means set to musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary ghost ship and its captain doomed to sail forever; a flier from Holland; Wagner's opera begins with it reaching Norway.

clue.text: Provide means of support for some heathen down south

indicators.note: some means part of, so the letters are found inside these words

explanation.surface: A request to fund a pagan who lives in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks letters out of 'heathen down'; 'south' says the run reads downward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give a lasting income to, such as funding a college post.

clue.text: Make out record on the computer that's left

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed after, the record coming first

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: left means gone away, so the letters for that's are removed

parts.note: ERNIE is the UK computer that picks Premium Bond winners
that is, abbreviated ie

explanation.surface: A record placed on the computer that someone left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the machine that draws Britain's Premium Bond prizes; 'left' removes IE (that is) from it, leaving ERN.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern is to perceive or distinguish, which is what making out means.

clue.text: Poetry of a Welshman about a New England state

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the Welshman's name goes round the state

parts.note: Rhys is a typical Welsh man's name
ME is the postal code for Maine

explanation.surface: Verse by a man from Wales about life in Maine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhymes is a loose term for verse, as in nursery rhymes.

clue.text: Alexander's application for a break?

parts.note: Alexander is another name of the Trojan prince who abducted Helen, and a fractured limb needs a set cast

explanation.surface: Something a man called Alexander applied for, perhaps a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trojan prince was also called Alexander (Alexandros), so his property is the setting material used on broken bones.
explanation.definitionFit: This white powder mixed with water sets hard, used for casts on fractures.

clue.text: Song cycle a university rejected

parts.note: a round is a cycle, one complete circuit

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the university's name is read backwards

parts.note: Yale is the American Ivy League university

explanation.surface: A song cycle is turned down by a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns YALE into ELAY; 'a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundelay is a short simple song with a refrain, an old word for a ditty.

clue.text: Dull as Guiderius's golden lads and girls, eventually?

definitions.text: as Guiderius's golden lads and girls, eventually

explanation.surface: A comment on a Shakespearean prince's fair young friends growing dull in time.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cymbeline, Guiderius sings 'Golden lads and girls all must, As chimney-sweepers, come to dust'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull colour is called dusty, drab and faded; the song's young people end up turned to dust, so covered in it.

clue.text: Son is held improperly — a feature of the defence

definitions.note: singular wording stands for the plural answer, a collective feature of armour

indicators.note: improperly means wrongly arranged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A son is detained unlawfully, a point made by his lawyers in defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improperly' rearranges IS HELD into HIELDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shields are protective armour carried by soldiers, a chief piece of their defensive kit.

clue.text: In the middle of which we're completely isolated

definitions.text: In the middle of which we're completely isolated

parts.words: In the middle of which we're completely isolated
parts.note: the idiom 'in the middle of ...' for a remote spot completes this sentence

explanation.surface: Someone describes a place so remote that they feel cut off from everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'in the middle of' this place is the stock phrase for total remoteness.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being far from any town says you are in the middle of no place at all.

clue.text: Order of electrically charged particles

explanation.surface: A sequence of charged particles in physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the classical architectural orders, and also the adjective for ions, the charged particles.

clue.text: Wind up universal combine? It's permanent

parts.note: to wind up is to end
U is the film certificate for universal viewing
a combine is a trading group, a ring or cartel

explanation.surface: A question of whether a worldwide cartel will ever wind up, since it seems permanent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combine' looks like a verb or farm machine but is a noun for a cartel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lasting is enduring, a near synonym for permanent.

clue.text: Figure reportedly ruined one of the first to settle

indicators.note: reportedly means as said, so the word for ruined is given by its sound

parts.note: ruined means wrecked

parts.words: one of the first to settle
parts.note: the Angles were Germanic settlers of early England

explanation.surface: A reported account of someone ruined, one of the early colonists.
explanation.walkthrough: The Angles, with the Saxons, settled England after the Romans left.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle is a four-sided geometric figure with right angles.

clue.text: Woman delivered article for a writer

parts.note: she is a pronoun for a woman
delivered means freed, rid
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman hands over a piece she wrote for an author.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheridan is the Irish playwright of The Rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Brinsley Sheridan was an eighteenth-century playwright, so a writer.

clue.text: Soundly thrash and grub about for something to eat

indicators.note: soundly means by sound, so the word for thrash is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: to thrash is to beat
to grub about is to root, as a pig does

explanation.surface: An instruction to beat someone hard and then rummage for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' qualifying thrash, but it signals the homophone BEET for BEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetroot is a red root vegetable eaten cooked or pickled.

clue.text: Internal transmitter broadcast a murder

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio report announces a killing.
explanation.definitionFit: The membrane inside the ear passes sound vibrations on to the inner ear, so transmits them.

clue.text: Many a pained cry from a patient supporter

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
ouch is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: Lots of people crying out in pain from a hospital bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'patient' is a psychoanalyst's patient, who lies on this.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychiatrist's patient traditionally lies on a couch, which supports them.

clue.text: Like Keats's sweeter melodies, not attracting an audience

explanation.surface: A comment on poetic music so sweet that nobody comes to listen.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats's Ode on a Grecian Urn says 'Heard melodies are sweet, but those unheard are sweeter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats praised melodies never actually heard; something not listened to has gone unnoticed.

clue.text: Extremely aloof, greyish .Asian hound?

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so take first and last letters of each word

explanation.surface: A haughty grey dog from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes the first and last letters of aloof, greyish and Asian: AF, GH, AN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Afghan is a long-haired breed of hunting dog, a hound.

clue.text: High platform — warning to passengers at the entrance

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
taken as written

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter, so take the opening letter of passengers

explanation.surface: A notice on a raised platform warning boarding passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretop is the platform at the head of a sailing ship's foremast, high above deck.

clue.text: Slug with a left — it's all that's needed

parts.note: a slug of spirits is a tot

explanation.surface: A boxer's punch with the left hand is all it takes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slug' looks like a punch, but it is a measure of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The total is the whole amount, every bit of it.

clue.text: What to do if she complains of the cold?

definitions.text: What to do if she complains of the cold?

parts.words: What to do if she complains of the cold?
parts.note: read as two words, the remedy for a chilly woman is to warm her up

explanation.surface: Advice on what to do when a woman says she is cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words it says what to do to her; whole it is a moorland shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Heather, the purple moorland plant, splits into a verb for warming and a pronoun for a woman.

clue.text: Wood for Ben's tee, say

parts.note: Ben's surname is Hur, as in Ben-Hur, so Ben's gives Hur's

indicators.note: say means as spoken, so tee stands for the letter it sounds like

parts.note: tee is how the letter T is said

explanation.surface: Timber to make a golf tee for someone called Ben.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben-Hur, the chariot-racing hero of the novel and film, supplies Hur.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurst is an old word for a wooded hill or copse, found in English place names.

clue.text: A rare drug prepared for backward soldiers

indicators.note: a drug prepared is made up, so these letters are made up anew

explanation.surface: A scarce medicine is made up for slow-witted troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' looks like slow, but means at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The rearguard is the body of soldiers protecting the back of an army.

clue.text: Indescribable, not having a handle

explanation.surface: Something beyond words, like a cup without a handle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nameless means too dreadful to describe, and also lacking a name, since a handle is slang for a name.

clue.text: Band to take care of before acting

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: to take care of is to tend
on means acting, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: A band looks after itself before going on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is a band of tough tissue joining muscle to bone.
